quest.title: The Servant's Path
quest.description: Blinded by fury, you fall into a trap laid by Scaramouche. But as you are about to black out, you catch a glimpse of Yae Miko's form...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x450, Mora x22000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Repeat after me. "Three, two, one, one, two, three, ahhhh, ahhhh." Come on.

choices.text: Three, two, one, one, two, three, ahhhh, ahhhh.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Okay, that's positive. Your brain seems relatively unscathed, this is good news.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It's just as well, really, with the amount of effort it took me to get you back here. Honestly, it was like you were glued to the ground back there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Miko, Paimon's been wanting to ask you about something. How come you're acting so differently from when we first met you?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Am I? Maybe it's because I had the other shrine maidens leave. Anyway, I've always been like this.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: People show you whatever side of themselves they want you to see. I know this for a fact.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Every side of me is the real me. People just like to define things in all sorts of arbitrary ways.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: This is a human society — at the moment, anyway — and I'm just doing as I please.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon didn't quite follow.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, study humans a while longer, my little friend. You'll see what I mean.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! Paimon was so focused on the Traveler that Paimon didn't notice what you did to get Scaramouche off our backs...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: What if I told you it was a secret art from the Grand Narukami Shrine, and that I had The Balladeer down on his knees begging for mercy in an instant... Would you believe me?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, well, maybe you should be worrying less about that and more about how exactly you are going to thank me... no?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm, maybe some of your neural circuitry is less intact than I thought...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you ever so much, Yae-sama.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I didn't mean you had to be so formal about it. I need your actions, not your words, hehe.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Delusions... they're still on your mind, aren't they?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You needn't worry. The leader of Watatsumi Island took some troops to clear the place out. She's also issued a strict ban on the use of Delusions across the whole army.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: With their stronghold exposed, I doubt The Balladeer is stubborn enough to try and retaliate now on his colleagues' behalf. It would be more trouble than it's worth.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ah, I must say, I would relish the opportunity to watch the Fatui getting a taste of their own medicine...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well anyway, that Sangonomiya Kokomi, she really outdid herself this time. I'd love to have another chat with her again in person, but alas... belief systems can be such a hindrance sometimes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A hindrance? Should you really be saying that as the guuji of the Grand Shrine!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Anyway. I'm only telling you this to stop you worrying, so that you can focus... on something I need you to do for me.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You've... met her, right?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'm not talking about the puppet. I mean... her. You've met her, yes?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. The true Raiden Shogun, who meditates endlessly in the Plane of Euthymia to preserve her being...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Her name is "Ei."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you saying that the one we met at the ceremony was just a puppet? And the real Raiden Shogun is the one that the Traveler met later?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And does that mean that when the battlefield changed... so did the opponent?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Because this is the Raiden Shogun's eternity.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Before pursuing the eternity of her nation, she had to reach eternity for herself.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Since the physical body will eventually turn to dust, she replaced hers with that of a puppet.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And since the spirit is susceptible to erosion, she placed her consciousness inside her sword, where she remains in a meditative state, free from all disturbances.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, that place that she carved open with her sword...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Plane of Euthymia. Essentially, the world inside her mind. A place that typically only allows her existence.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: She shuts herself off in her inner world, leaving all the affairs of the outside world to be dealt with by a puppet who has a singular focus on the pursuit of eternity...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...This is the approach Ei has come up with for realizing eternity.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You mean Morax? It's been a while since I last saw him. A surprising decision by Liyue's archon... what a fascinating god he is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It seems like the Raiden Shogun's approach solves the problem Zhongli was facing though...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, perhaps... or you could take the view that she's acting like a little child, throwing a temper tantrum and locking herself in her room. Don't you think?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The grand notion of eternity she once held has long since given way to the eternity of her own definition.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And ultimately, her eternity is defined by fear... the fear of loss.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm still not sure what you want me to do.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The truth is... we are on the same side.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You want to save the people of Inazuma from the Vision Hunt Decree. So do I. The only difference is that I'd rather like to save this nation and save Ei while we're at it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The key is that the Plane of Euthymia represents Ei's inner world. Defeat her there and you may well have the chance to shake the Raiden Shogun's will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this is your plan to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not by talking her out of it, or through an armed resistance, but by uh... hopping inside the Raiden Shogun's inner world?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You're a fast learner. In short, this is the last chance to get Inazuma back on track. Otherwise, an eternity of darkness awaits.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Don't you realize how special you are? Remember, the Plane of Euthymia is a space where only she is allowed to exist. The fact that you could appear there tells us one crucial thing:

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That you have piqued her interest. Perhaps it's because... she has never seen an individual who is so unpredictable in the face of eternity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Has no one else ever been in there?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: None. No one has seen the devotee of eternity since she shut herself away. In fact, no one even knows what it looks like in there.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Your existence is more than just an opportunity. It's the very key to all of this. To that I say... well done, child, you did not disappoint me after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you're leaving? Where are you going?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>Anti-Raiden Shogun Training</color>. I've prepared a special program, just for you. Come along now.

choices.text: It's one reason why he stepped down.
But why go to such lengths?
So this is why you rescued me?
How did you save me from The Balladeer?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh? You recognized me right away. Your brain seems relatively unscathed, this is good news.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're gonna do it here? And what's this <color=#00E1FFFF>mechanism</color> for?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Think of it as a catalyst that can reproduce the Raiden Shogun's combat moves. I made it from my own memory, which means it should be perfectly accurate — unless of course, her skills have declined.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It'll give you a chance to figure out her moves in advance and come up with a counter strategy. That should be a big help, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The aim is to try not to get hit by the attacks. Since you've escaped certain death at her hand once already, I presume this shouldn't be more than you can handle?

talks.objective: Complete the Anti-Raiden Shogun Training (on any difficulty)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, what a workout...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So how come you know so much about the Raiden Shogun?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm, you mean me?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Perhaps it's because... I'm the Electro Archon's familiar.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Like Dvalin is to Barbatos? Never would have guessed by looking at you...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, it sounds like you'd be more persuaded if you saw me in my fox form?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In your dreams.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: More curious than my appearance is the fact that she and I don't see each other anymore, wouldn't you say?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: "A nation to last for all eternity" is a dream that she and I both share. But I don't think that's the same thing as complete stasis.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: At some point, she started going down a path that became increasingly difficult for me to join her on.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You know, Ei never said goodbye to me before she stepped into the Plane of Euthymia.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Perhaps it's just my wishful thinking, but I think she did this deliberately, as her way of keeping our friendship eternal.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: By neither saying goodbye nor seeing me again, our relationship will remain forever how it was... in her mind, at least.

choices.text: The Raiden Shogun is the wishful thinker here.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Since we've embarked on two very different paths to eternity, I can either continue to maintain the status quo or do whatever it takes to bring her back on track, regardless of the cost...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I have chosen the latter because... if stubbornly isolating herself in the Plane of Euthymia is her idea of eternity...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Then my duty as her eternal familiar is to drag her back out of her own head and into the real world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, Miko... you sound like a really great friend.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Heh, I'm only telling you this so you can properly understand my plan. Could you possibly spare the sentimentality for the time being?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Anyway, that's enough chit-chat. Time for <color=#00E1FFFF>Anti-Raiden Shogun Training Phase 2</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a part 2!?

choices.text: She has taken a very one-sided view.

talks.objective: Complete the next phase of your Anti-Raiden Shogun Training

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... we're finally done. How did we do?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You did quite admirably. I could see your determination and your hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So do you think we're ready to beat the Raiden Shogun now?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: How do I put this... you're no match for her at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what!? So all of this was a complete waste of time!?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe. You are the most important part of the plan. I know what I'm doing. You don't think I'd leave you with no chance to win at all, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Speaking of... Traveler, what do you think of the resistance army's chances?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hah, you're absolutely right. Perhaps they occasionally best the Shogun's Army in open battle, but when they face the Raiden Shogun herself...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Considering even their Visions have been taken from them and embedded in the Statue, they are ultimately quite helpless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't have to be so blunt. The Traveler's the captain of Swordfish II, y'know!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe. I don't mean to belittle them. On the contrary...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It is precisely because of their helplessness, because their Visions have been taken from them, that their will is all the more precious.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In short, if everything goes according to plan, they may yet prove to be helpful.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... what is the plan?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh... goodness, is that the time? I have another guest to receive today. We can talk more back at the <color=#00E1FFFF>Grand Narukami Shrine</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All of a sudden you're entertaining guests!? Paimon's really struggling to understand how you work...

choices.text: They're no match for her either.

talks.objective: Return to the Grand Narukami Shrine and talk to Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Okay, we can talk here. You asked me about the plan — in fact, I've been mulling it over for quite a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Before one makes a plan, what is the most important thing one must do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't know, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You must understand the situation you are facing.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The Vision Hunt Decree was obviously devised as a means of manipulating the Shogun, the ones behind it knowing full well her susceptibility as a puppet with a single-minded focus on eternity.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. This is the strongest piece of evidence we have to go on.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Now, we also know that every aspect of the Vision Hunt Decree's promulgation and execution has been enthusiastically spearheaded by the Tenryou Commission from the outset.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ayaka was saying that every time they submitted a petition against the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions would veto it straight away with no negotiation.

choices.text: The Tenryou Commission is working for the Fatui.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes. It's all too clear that both the Tenryou and Kanjou Commissions are in some form of collusion with the Fatui. Hmph, foolish humans, blinded by their greed.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Thus, the current situation is that our Fatui antagonist is still at large, has the two rogue Commissions wrapped around their finger, and is distributing Delusions from the shadows...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Unfortunately, given that said antagonist is under the protection of two Commissions and the Raiden Shogun, we would be rather hard-pressed to track them down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what should we do?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: It will be easier for us to start with someone from Inazuma.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: So my plan is... to incite rebellion in the Tenryou Commission.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rebellion? What are you talking about? After everything you just said, it sounds like the Tenryou Commission has rebelled already!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe. When I say rebellion, I don't mean betraying the Shogunate... I mean, inciting a certain someone to betray the Tenryou Commission.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: If we manage to convince her, I'm quite sure we'll be able to get you another audience with the Raiden Shogun.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I'll give you a clue: She's currently in charge of the Shogun's Army, she visits the shrine at this time every month, and she is our guest today.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: She also appears to be standing right behind you.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Don't move a muscle! You've got some nerve showing up here in the shrine when there's an active warrant for your arrest!

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: #Don't even think about trying anything. Surrender now, you're coming with me to headquarters. Seize {F#her}{M#him}!

response.speaker: Motosuke
response.text: Affirmative!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: K—Kujou Sara!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Uh-uh-uh, it seems that you're forgetting, this is the Grand Narukami Shrine...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Use of force here is strictly forbidden. Before you proceed, which of you would like to face criminal charges for dishonoring the Shogun, hmm?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Ugh.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Guuji Yae... please tell me you are not sheltering a wanted criminal here?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: We are just friends, I don't see what sheltering has to do with it. Tell your subordinates to leave, we have things to discuss.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: All of you, outside.

response.speaker: Sue Yoshitaka
response.text: As you wish.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Guuji Yae, I'm a little curious — does it not also dishonor the Shogun to hide a wanted criminal at her grand shrine?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehehe... You are the same as ever, Kujou Sara. No one can match you when it comes to loyalty to the Shogun.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: As a servant, loyalty to the Shogun is my duty. And as a warrior, I dedicate my life to following the way of the Shogun.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Even though she will one day... seize your Vision, too?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: The Vision Hunt Decree is the Shogun's chosen course, and I shall not question it.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* It's tragic... such wholehearted devotion, rendered meaningless by circumstance. Have you been kept in the dark? Or are you the only one left in the light?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Lady Guuji, I need you to be direct. Tell me exactly what you mean.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Vision Hunt Decree is a trap. Part of a Fatui plot to bring Inazuma to its knees.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And your masters, the Kujou Clan of the Tenryou Commission — they are the ones keeping the truth from reaching the Shogun.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: You're saying the Kujou Clan... betrayed the Shogunate?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Yes, that's exactly what I'm saying.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Guuji Yae, your allegation is not only dangerous but ridiculous. The Tri-Commission has served the Shogun since ancient times and remains absolutely loyal to this day.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Ever since I was adopted by the Kujou Clan, I have seen and heard nothing but pure devotion toward the Shogun. At every level of the Tenryou Commission — especially from the head of the clan, Kujou Takayuki...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: He reveres the Musou no Hitotachi more than anyone. My own respect for the Shogun pales in comparison to his.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: How could he ever even dream of acting against the Shogun?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Three days... come back here in three days, and I will show you the evidence.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As a Guuji, there's one thing I know very well: People believe whatever they want to believe. Some things you do not see, simply because you do not wish to look.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: And so... it falls to me to place the truth before your eyes, in all its ugliness.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Hmph... three days? I'll be here. But if I don't see any evidence, I will demand a formal apology for slandering the Kujou Clan. Also...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: #...{F#She}{M#He} will have to come with me.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Wonderful. Then I'll see you in three days. I look forward to it very much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was so scary. Paimon wasn't expecting to run into Kujou Sara here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Miko, you mentioned evidence of the Tenryou Commission's betrayal. Is that all in hand and good to go, or...?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Why are you always asking so many questions? Of course not. I just had to say something because I clearly wasn't convincing her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... not entirely unexpected.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: As plans go, changing the deity's mind is a huge gamble to begin with. We can't expect to be in control of every last detail when we're facing off against a god, can we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, but what are we gonna do though? We only have three days!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: If we want to get our evidence, we're going to need some help. Now... come with me. We must awaken <color=#00E1FFFF>the professional</color>.

choices.text: The Kanjou Commission betrayed the Shogunate long ago.
The Fatui did it to create the demand for Delusions.

talks.objective: Return to the Grand Narukami Shrine and talk to Yae Miko

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's stopping you? Not still traumatized from your last encounter, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: If you get hit by the Musou no Hitotachi, that's it. It's game over. I would get training if I were you.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Well, that was an interesting poem.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Already understand?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hehe... I am your teacher, after all. It wouldn't be much good if my mind couldn't keep up with my students'.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: But you should understand it however it makes sense to you. My little wolf cub will improve much more quickly that way.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm much more suited to leisurely days like these...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I'd love to, cutie. Hmm, too bad I can't offer you some tea.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I was quite surprised to learn that the Grand Master had written a private message just for me.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: And I was equally surprised to find out that Razor's been on his mind this whole time.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Especially given how demanding he is of Jean... He left her to figure out the whole Weinlesefest on her own, and didn't give her a single word of acknowledgment.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I'll have to have to a stern word with him on Jean's behalf when he returns.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: It's funny — I always thought the Grand Master was the one who gave him the name "Razor"...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: But it turns out his birth parents chose it all along.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Anyway, Razor told me he heard the voices of his parents during the festival.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: "Like stepping on a rock in the sun. Warm, but also heavy."

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I'm sure he must think of them as both kind and dauntless people...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Originally, I only planned on having a glass or two. I thought I deserved a treat after being such a good teacher recently.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: But that was before I came to appreciate how truly exceptional the festival-exclusive vintage was...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Before I knew it, I was already rather tipsy, hehe...

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: I'm a bad example. Don't be like me, cutie.

response.speaker: Lisa
response.text: Alright, but remember, it's important to rest when you're feeling tired. It makes my heart ache to see you so busy all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I didn't expect you to come by here. Unless... oh, were you following the fragrance of wine on the wind?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Sure, the sound of your voice is always a pleasure to hear.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Blessings? Oh, that.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Between you and me... I breathed a sigh of relief when nobody said their wishes out loud during the toast. That would've really put me in a tough spot. Hahaha... The Anemo Archon, Barbatos, doesn't have unlimited power, you know.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I had to take a really deep breath to get the winds of the far-flung past blowing. I nearly went blue in the face.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He's grown up so much recently... It's such a joy to see.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Huh... Suddenly I sound just like an old grandpa.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: He was lucky to have friends like you ready to support him through all this.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I see a kind, gentle soul, with a healthy dose of romance and freedom, too... In other words, a true Mondstadter, who grew up drinking the water of Cider Lake.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You, on the other hand... Don't worry, you're the gentlest soul I've ever met.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Oh, I've been very busy on that front. I'd long since drunk my fill by Windcoming Day.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But, uh, I wasn't counting on everyone bringing out their finest vintage to welcome me.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, the fragrance alone was so intoxicating... I had no choice but to make room for a few more rounds...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Full disclosure — I also secretly hid two bottles away for myself at the end.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Then go, my friend. The stories that unfolded here shall be remembered by the wind in the form of verse.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: The wind is gentle, comfortable.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: The message in the letter... I want to thank him.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...I miss him. Lupical miss him, too.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Now, I am grown up.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I want to hear him talk about human father and mother.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Their voices. I heard them.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Human father and mother... were adventurers...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Teacher said, maybe they didn't survive...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Aw, Razor...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I have a wooden box. Inside are treasures from my friends.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: They are, most precious things I own.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Inside box from human father and mother... is all about me...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: A long time ago, I thought I was alone. Only have lupical.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Now, I know many people.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Everyone helps me. I will help everyone, too.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Humans, wolves, everyone.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: I am the bridge between city and outside.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay. You go enjoy the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: So, what do you think of the Weinlesefest? Have you enjoyed yourself?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Well, what would you like to know?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: *sigh* I can sympathize with the anguish of being away from family.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Certainly, a tragic situation. But tragedy can also drive personal growth, and perhaps learning how to face it head-on is part of growing up... part of becoming an adult.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Having the support of some good friends will certainly make that journey easier.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: ...When I unsealed the wine, it seemed that the words of my late father were sealed inside.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I wonder what he would think if he were to see me now.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Somehow, I doubt he'd share the same view as he did back then.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course he would.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Heh...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: If you say so.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: To the people of Mondstadt, wine-making is a way of working through emotions, and remembering our history.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: We're only able to make such high-quality wines these days thanks to the peace we enjoy. War is a thing of the distant past.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Even though you might not see me reveling with the crowds, I am grateful for this as much as anyone.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Say, have you tried our latest product, "Fruits of the Festival"?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: If you have any thoughts on how it could be improved, I'm all ears.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Sure. We'll talk when you're free.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, hello again...

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Sure. Did you have something you wanted to ask me about?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Oh. Yes, I read his letter. Barbara showed it to me.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: She'd been so worried about her father, Seamus. She almost burst into tears when she read that "the expedition is safe and all of its members are accounted for."

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Hmm? ...My thoughts?

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Hehe... You're curious what he means to me as a father figure, is that right? Well, I guess I'm not like other daughters. I can't bring myself to worry about him.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: He wouldn't be leading that many people if he didn't have the necessary strength and courage for it. He's not the kind of person you need to worry about.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: So, he's finally come to terms with everything?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: At the very least, he's no longer lost and confused.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He has a direction now.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Hmm, sounds like he still has some way to go before he can say he's fully independent. But everyone goes through their own life in their own way.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Well done. It sounds like your efforts were all worth it in the end.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I thought that if I made it to the Weinlesefest, I'd have the chance to spend a whole day in the tavern. Turns out, there's actually more work during a festival than usual.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: I managed to escape to here, but I still can't completely let my guard down. Who knows when Victoria or Dahlia might show up and drag me off to the sung poetry event.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: *sigh* The sooner this festival is over, the better.

response.speaker: Rosaria
response.text: Alright. But don't tell anyone else that I'm here. I don't want to have to move anytime soon.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hi there, are you here to take a look at my stall? I have a lot of newly developed research products.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Um, okay, go ahead...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh, this?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I actually wrote out all the nutritional information and prices for my Bio-Alchemy products in advance. But the customers still prefer to ask directly...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: So... I just read off the sheet for them...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Running a stall is a huge challenge for me.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Maybe I could get Noelle to interact with the customers, and I do the rest... Mmm, no, never mind... She's probably busy enough already.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I have here the Iota-Series Rapid-Acting Deep Freeze Mist Flower, the Theta-Series Fragrance-Enhanced Sweet Flower, Variation 21...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: And the Epsilon-Series Tetrasweet Sunsettia, Variation 63. I'm proud to put my name to all of these products!

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: You won't need me to read out all the details, right?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I'm sorry for running off back then...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I just thought that you and Noelle would do a better job of expressing things than I could...

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Did everything work out in the end? Mixing the Epsilon-Series Tetrasweet Sunsettia, Variation 63 with the other ingredients didn't cause any problems, did it?

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh, and uh... how did things go with Razor...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Don't worry. Everything turned out great.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Phew... Thank goodness.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Then... can I ask you for a favor? I want to make a note of the full recipe for the Thousand-Wind Wine we made.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: That way, we'll be able to recreate the exact same flavor we did today in the future, no matter how many years go by.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Oh, sure. No problem.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Are you here to set up a booth, too?

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: The wine market is being held outside of Springvale this time. Not only is the scenery gorgeous, but delivering goods there is pretty convenient.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: But since we — that is, Angel's Share — have a large booth, it takes quite a long time to get everything set up.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Would you like something to drink? Not only are we selling wine, but we are also acquiring all kinds of wine-making ingredients during the festival. You're welcome to come around and discuss anything you're interested in.

dialogues.speaker: Leah
dialogues.text: Forest boars make regular appearances during the harvest season, so you have to take extra care when delivering goods.

dialogues.speaker: Leah
dialogues.text: The Knight of Favonius and Springvale's hunters have already come up with a plan to drive the forest boars off. I hear that a youth who can talk to wolves will come and help as well...

dialogues.speaker: Leah
dialogues.text: Welcome to Weinlesefest! If there's anything you need help with, please contact the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Leah
response.text: Well, speaking of that, there's actually no requirement a location has to meet to host it. This celebratory event has been held in Mondstadt City itself several times before as well.

response.speaker: Leah
response.text: But personally, I prefer the site that they selected this year. Compared to the hustle and bustle of the city, Cider Lake has prettier scenery and a more rustic charm.

response.speaker: Leah
response.text: As one of the festival's sponsors, the Knights of Favonius will maintain order on-site while ensuring that every guest will enjoy the festivities to the fullest.

response.speaker: Leah
response.text: As such, I'd also like to remind our guests to drink in moderation! Over-drinking and bothering other guests will result in a visit from us.

response.speaker: Leah
response.text: Bye, enjoy the festival!

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: Sorry, but Diona will be on leave for the duration of the festival... Oh, you're not here to see Diona? That's rare.

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: Come and buy some fresh fruit! All of them are freshly picked and suitable for eating or wine-making!

dialogues.speaker: Marcel
dialogues.text: I'll let you in on a little secret — at least half of the apples that Dawn Winery uses to make their Apple Cider come from us.

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "Our booth sells old books that the library regularly phases out. These books will not have missing pages and will not be torn, but they may show signs of age. Thanks for your understanding."

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "All books are on sale at half price. All proceeds will go towards the total earnings of the Knights of Favonius' charity sale, which will be used to help Mondstadt residents in need."

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "The vendor is out on business. Please take any books you need and place the money in the wooden box under the booth."

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: All your general goods sold here at affordable prices, come and take a look!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: Well, if it isn't the Honorary Knight! It's a pleasure to meet you!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: I was doing business abroad previously, and I normally only come back during Weinlesefest. It's no surprise that we haven't met before.

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: If it's meant to be, I'm sure we'll meet again elsewhere!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: Not bad at all!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: As you can see, Weinlesefest is swarming with guests! I can make as much in one day here as I normally would in four or five!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: I wish there were more lively festivals like this one!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: See you, may we meet again!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: We sell all sorts of fresh flowers and plants here — looking to buy a few bouquets?

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: Greetings, Honorary Knight!

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: Perhaps you don't recognize me...

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: But I'm a resident of Springvale, and I run a small flower shop.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: I'm always busy looking after the flowers and plants, so I haven't had any dealings with visitors from outside the town in a long time...

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: I never thought I'd meet a celebrity like you this year. Perhaps it's good luck brought by the returning wind?

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: I'm a keen gardener — the plants you see here? I grew them all myself. They're less common varieties that are purely ornamental.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: My hope is that such beautiful plants will lift everyone's spirits.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: However, because of their seasonal nature, I can only open for business at certain times of the year.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: Goodbye, have a nice day!

dialogues.speaker: Clemens
dialogues.text: I'm a winemaker from Sailing Breeze. I came to this market specifically to purchase ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Clemens
dialogues.text: You haven't heard of us at all? Heh, that's no surprise. We're an old brand, but we primarily do business overseas these days. We don't even have a shop in Mondstadt anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Clemens
dialogues.text: We can't compete with Dawn Winery, but Sailing Breeze has made quite a name for itself in Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Clemens
dialogues.text: That girl Karpillia was so desperate to expand into the overseas market, but it was the right call in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Clemens
dialogues.text: Thanks to her, my skills can still be put to good use even now.

dialogues.speaker: Lenne
dialogues.text: Weinlesefest is the best festival for bards!

dialogues.speaker: Lenne
dialogues.text: Sampling fine wines while singing your heart out. This is the life of a bard, and that's how it's supposed to be.

dialogues.speaker: Lenne
dialogues.text: It's the perfect festival for getting those creative juices flowing. I really hope my poet friends from Inazuma can come and check it out as well.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Yo, Honorary Knight! Would you like to hear good news from the shop?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the shop?

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Haha, let me break it down for you, and you can tell me what you think!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for your hard work!

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Saying that will out you as an outsider! It's not hard work, it's a good time!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Hello, do you have any new tasks?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the shop?

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: You'll be pleased to know that business has been doing great recently.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You've been working hard!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Thanks! I feel fulfilled to be able to do something for the elderly and the children!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: You're here! Would you like an update? Or, do you have a new business strategy?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the shop?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Everything is going well. Please listen to the business briefing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for your hard work!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: No worries, it's my honor to contribute to the charity sale!

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Yo, I heard the charity sale was a great success. Congratulations, Honorary Knight!

choices.text: This is the result of our collaborative efforts.

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: Hehe, good point!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: This event has invigorated me. We didn't make money, but we had more fun than ever.

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: I guess it's the satisfaction of doing a good deed.

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: Sure! I'm about to leave, too!

response.speaker: Mats
response.text: Next time I'll be sure to try harder!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, word around town is that the charity sale was a runaway success, all thanks to you, Paimon, Bernhard, and Mats!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Even I got a taste of the limelight, getting a few "thank you" notes of my own...

choices.text: This is the result of our collaborative efforts.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: I haven't done enough, not as much as you guys.

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: However, after listening to your business strategy, I felt I have learned a lot and have become a more skilled businesswoman!

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: Anyway, many thanks!

response.speaker: Pauline
response.text: Please make sure to look for me when you get the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: I'll take care of the shop's set-up. You two can focus on preparing the necessary funds!

choices.text: About how to prepare the funds...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: You could help nearby customers place orders with the wine merchants or supply winemakers with ingredients...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Either method is fine, so you can just prioritize based on your preference.

choices.text: About the person in charge being appointed through draws...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Well... The person in charge was determined by a random draw mechanism that was intended to give each Knight an equal chance... to facilitate dialogue between us and the public...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: I can do my usual work just fine. But when it comes to deciding on a direction or coming up with a plan, I'm always afraid that I'll make a mess of things...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: So, it's a good thing that you, our Honorary Knight, have stepped up to the plate! You could say that you saved this charity event — not to mention me!

choices.text: Let me give it a try first!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Okay! I'm looking forward to hearing the good news from you.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: I'd like to buy some beverages.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Here's the menu.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to sell wine-making ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Sure, these are the ingredients that we're buying at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About this booth...

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Angel's Share participates in Weinlesefest each time, and plenty of folk come all the way here to Mondstadt to sample our limited-edition wines.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Back when Master Crepus was around, he'd come to us in person every year to drink a glass...

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: *sigh* I don't know why, but this festival always makes me nostalgic.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: Diluc... I mean, Master Diluc has had a rough go of it these past few years, but he seems to be in good spirits this year.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: As long as Master Diluc is well, I'm sure Master Crepus' spirit up above will also be pleased.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Georg
dialogues.text: See you. Come back any time!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, Paimon, you've been running the shop for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: The current operation method of the store refers to the previous business activities, which is fine, but may not be applicable in all cases.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: You are well informed and can think about your unique "business style" based on your experience with other business people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Is this what Bernhard meant earlier when he mentioned "Shop Stratagems"?

choices.text: We actually have quite a few ideas.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Okay! Then do whatever you feel is best, and I will do my best to carry out your orders!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: At the same time, I will also help collect the experience of other businessmen and provide it to you.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: I hope these notes will inspire you and give you new ideas!

choices.text: It's time to put them into practice.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight and Paimon, the "owner's assessment" is here. Please cooperate with me!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Owner's assessment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds a bit like a legal examination. Are we supposed to fill out a... super-complicated answer sheet?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: No no no. No need to be so formal. I just need your verbal answers!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Our store was in a special situation, and Leah was supposed to be inspecting me, but I already knew the entire safety manual by heart.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: You two are in charge now, so Leah asked me to check you out on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: All you have to do is answer two questions and prove that you are safety-aware. I believe in you guys!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: You can also get a reward if you answer correctly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon was really nervous about the test just now! Well, now it sounds pretty simple.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Alright. First question.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: "If a known alcoholic suddenly shows up in front of your shop intoxicated, what do you do?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! That's definitely wrong!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Well... the correct answer is "call the Knights of Favonius for support to prevent the other party from getting into a drunken accident"...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Still, according to the Honorary Knight's thinking, if it can fuddle even an alcoholic like that, it must be no ordinary drink.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Its stock is bound to be limited. If we join in, we can cut down on inventory in other stores.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Plus, there's another place on the market that sells it. It reduces the likelihood that drinkers will drink too much in one store.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Amazing! Thinking longer-term is indeed something more fitting for the Honorary Knight!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Bernhard... This logic is so complicated... You don't have to work so hard to bail {NICKNAME} out...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Alright, so next question...

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: "Items for sale are often boxed up and stacked, posing a fire hazard. As a shopkeeper, what measures would you take to prevent fire hazards?"

choices.text: Put a Cryo Slime in one of the boxes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Be serious!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Wait, I never thought about that before!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: The way goods are stacked for sale is a problem that every shopkeeper faces.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Normally, a good answer would be along the lines that "it is very dangerous to concentrate a large number of wooden boxes together, and they should be stacked separately with proper ventilation in mind."

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: But that would make it cumbersome to pick up the goods, and it would be too much of a problem for understaffed stores.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Only those who are very strong can employ the Honorary Knight's method. But by ensuring the fire resistance of wooden cases, you can fundamentally solve the problem.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: I remembered Timaeus in the city say that there is a coating laced with Slime Condensate that has a good fire resistance effect. That's for sure worth promoting!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bernhard... are you for real?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #If Paimon knew {NICKNAME} could answer either way, Paimon would have jumped on those questions, immediately!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Otherwise, as one of the store owners, Paimon isn't pulling any weight at all!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Please don't be discouraged, Paimon. The Honorary Knight's answers were light and witty, and also made sense. In a way, it's a lot like what you would say.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Perhaps the Honorary Knight's answers to the questions were inspired by you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, really?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, that's right. Next time you have a question like that, let Paimon answer it.

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: Either way, I always learn a lot when I'm working with you two!

response.speaker: Bernhard
response.text: You passed! You gave excellent answers to both questions. Here is the reward from Leah, please accept it!

choices.text: Put a Cryo Slime in each of the boxes...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: You two! We've got a problem!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: An unidentified man came quietly into the store, leaving a package and a letter.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: The man said in his letter that he had heard about our charity sale, and remembered his financial hardships as a child. He was very touched.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: He wanted every child to grow up happy, so he donated some Fairbrew Jelly and other goods for sale.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the first time this has happened to us! Paimon's a little moved...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But... why would he hide his identity?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe this guy has a low profile! Perhaps, doing good deeds without leaving a name also gives a special sense of accomplishment?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Maybe we should be more prudent...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: I have heard that Treasure Hoarders have mixed counterfeit goods with ordinary goods for unsuspecting merchants to sell.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: This way, they can successfully throw away the hot potato, and make Mora on the side.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can't believe it! Those horrible Treasure Hoarders, how can they even cheat innocent shop owners and customers!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon's suddenly a little nervous... {NICKNAME}, what do you think we should do with the package...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This will not affect the sales revenue.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Indeed, Knights of Favonius has done this before - auctioning off the loot of Treasure Hoarders to raise money for charity.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Even if the package's origins are questionable, it's all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, the Treasure Hoarders wouldn't dare do this in a Knight of Favonius' shop, would they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, he just left the package and it didn't seem like he made half a Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: People who are willing to follow the charity sale must be very kind, and we don't have to be so nervous!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Then we'll take this package. I'll make a note of it and report it to the head office.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Better check the package.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, let's be on the safe side!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: I'll take the package back to the Knights of Favonius and have it verified.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Bernhard took the package to the Knights of Favonius headquarters...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: It's approved, Honorary Knight and Paimon! There was nothing wrong with the content of the package!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Captain Hertha told us not to worry. In previous years, people have made such anonymous donations at the charity sale.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: But this is still a good reminder. Recently, we've been following the Treasure Hoarders very closely, and it's possible they could use this trick to get out of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: When Captain Hertha heard about it, she also made a donation to the sale from her own pocket to show her encouragement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sees... So the package is alright! Thanks to this mysterious kind soul. Paimon wishes him good fortune every day!

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: This won't do. There won't be any end to this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong, Mats? What's up with the store?

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: It's an old problem. I have some daily necessities that have been shipped to my store, and they've been caught in the middle of the wind, waves, and tide.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: I was hoping to dry them while we were open, in hopes that they would be ready to sell for cheap at the end of the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: But the sunshine in Mondstadt is too gentle, and we are here beside Cider Lake, where the air is humid. So far, nothing has gone as planned.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: If it goes on like this, our daily necessities will get moldy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... this is a bit tricky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe we can make a fire to dry the shipment... but that would be too dangerous... Bernhard and Leah would stop it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You could try using Flaming Flower Stamens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's a good idea. The Flaming Flower Stamens are really hot and should be able to dry them out in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To be on the safe side, you can also put them in a large glass bottle, so you don't have to worry about fire spreading.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Good idea. I'll send someone to get the needed materials!

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: You two are very clever, and I am in your debt!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How about using Anemograna?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean blowing the goods dry with the strong wind from the Anemograna?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... The wind will be strong enough for sure, but won't it blow the goods away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Perhaps we can tie the boxes together and increase their total weight that way!

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Huh. That's not a bad idea! I'll send someone to find Anemograna right now, and I'll send all the supplies over.

dialogues.speaker: Mats
dialogues.text: Thank you both very much. Please accept this as a token of my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Arranging flowers really is a science unto itself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you running into any problems, Pauline?

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: It's not really a big deal.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Usually, I always sell flowers by variety, because I think they would be clear to customers at a glance...

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: But recently, I heard that combining several kinds of flowers can make them complement each other and look more beautiful.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: I tried to match the different flowers, and although I don't quite understand how it works, the business of the shop during the festival is significantly more busy.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: So I was wondering, how do you cultivate this particular kind of artistic sense? Do you have to find a professional mentor?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, what Pauline said is definitely something worth thinking about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go with something that matches your inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, inspiration does work really well sometimes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, you put some random flowers together and that made the store's business better, just like that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that means that you're plenty inspired. Just follow your heart from now on, and maybe you won't need a mentor at all!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Really? This is the first time I've ever been told that... I seemed to have hit my stride!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Thank you for your vote of confidence! I don't know what to say, but I'd like to thank you properly...

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Here is a token of my gratitude. Please take it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go look for some reference books first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... theory is the safest way to get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Knights of Favonius' library has a large collection of books. You should be able to find something there, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Liyue and Inazuma also have knowledge on arranging flowers. If you get the chance, you can also try to get some books written there for reference.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: I understand. I'll ask someone to help me get some books from the library once Weinlesefest ends.

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: As for reference books from Liyue and Inazuma, I should be able to ask Mats. He travels a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, maybe the next time we meet, you'll have become a master at arranging flowers!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: I'll do my best. Your suggestions are really valuable. Thank you very much!

dialogues.speaker: Pauline
dialogues.text: Here is a token of my gratitude. Please take it!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight. Paimon. There's one more thing for you to decide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, alright. We'll help. What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: The peak time of Weinlesefest will soon be over. Some shopkeepers estimate that they will have some surplus in stock and plan to donate to us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't that a good thing? "Surplus stock" sounds like a bad thing, but they seem to mean well.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We might not be able to sell it all.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: The Honorary Knight has a good point. Our ability to sell is also limited.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: After these goods are donated to us, we might not be able to sell them, and they might accumulate.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Some of the daily necessities and food would soon go bad, which would be a waste of good intentions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm! Paimon didn't think about that. {NICKNAME} always seems to know best!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Perhaps we should politely decline after explaining our reasons.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Understood. I'll talk to the owners.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Bernhard leaves to talk to the people involved...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight. Paimon. The owners were very reasonable and understood our reply.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: However, the shopkeepers did donate a sum of money to show their support for the charity sale.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These shopkeepers are so kind...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, it is fortunate that nothing went to waste this time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could it be resold to the Knights of Favonius?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: This is indeed a method, and sometimes, the Knights will spontaneously count their personal needs.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: If residents have used goods that they are willing to sell, and the knights do not mind, they can make a deal directly to reduce the waste of materials.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: In the same way, the inhabitants could speak directly to the knights if they need something.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Maybe someone recently wanted to buy something, but didn't realize that these owners had a lot of stuff they couldn't sell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Well, it's up to you to bridge the gap, Bernhard.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Bernhard leaves for the Order to look at the purchase needs...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight. Paimon. Good news!

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: It just so happens that a lot of people want to buy used goods these days, and they can resell most of the surplus goods to them.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Some of the knights also chipped in to pay for our hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! The thrift crisis is solved, and everyone's needs are met!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to sell wine-making ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: One moment please, let me have a look around for Miss Margaret's acquisition list. Now, where did I put it...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Diona and Margaret aren't here?

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: Yes, Miss Diona's mood tends to sour when Weinlesefest comes around, so Miss Margaret gave her some time off.

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: But that's understandable. After all, the number of booze hounds at the wine market far exceeds that which you might find at the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: As for Miss Margaret, she certainly wouldn't pass up the festivities just to run the business. She's probably off somewhere drinking and having a good time as we speak.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bye.

dialogues.speaker: Diane
dialogues.text: See you, happy Weinlesefest!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Quinn!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: ... It's you again, you're not gonna drag me into giving you another discount, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Before you say anything, I'm way too busy for this Weinlesefest!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Even if you're busy, you shouldn't forget about me!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: No matter fruit or fruit wine, for the sake of childhood friendship, can't you get me a discount?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: I've told you many times, the fruit is not on sale. And I'm just helping deliver fruit to the drink stands. How can you insist on a discount?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Come on, hook a sister up!

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I know you love wine. I'll get some and share with you. Then I'll help you make some refreshments. Could you just give me a discount?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: No discounts. No matter what you say!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Weinlesefest...

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Weinlesefest is an autumn festival to celebrate the harvest of the Mondstadters. We use the fruits of the harvest to make drinks to dedicate to the Anemo Archon. He will then bless everyone with the West Wind.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: That said, for Mondstadters, it doesn't matter whether Lord Barbatos actually shows up or not. The festival is just a good time to drink lots of wine.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Although drunk people are troublesome, I can't really say anything when I see nothing but uplifted spirits from drinking.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: After all, everyone has worked hard all year and deserves a good celebration.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Weinlesefest... is truly an amazing festival!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: If it never ended, everyone would be able to have Dawn Winery's Weinlesefest specialty every day...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Eh, I really needed this to relax and forget about that nag...

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Welcome to Floral Whisper. Do you need anything?

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Recently, everyone asked what flower best represents the happiness of harvest. Hehe, I think Dandelion is suitable.

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: Come in, come in! We are having a special Weinlesefest discount at Angel's Share!

dialogues.speaker: Patton
dialogues.text: If you pass by Springvale, don't forget to stop by our stand and have a look!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Mika...

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Oh? You've already met my brother? Then I don't think there's much to say.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: I was so worried about him when he went out with the Grand Master. But now it seems I was too worried.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Although he is still prone to shyness, his ability to survey and do mapping has improved a lot, and his work is done in short order.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: I hear he's joining the Guerrilla Assault platoon next, and he probably won't be back in town for a while. I wish him all the best!

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Welcome to Mondstadt, Traveler. Please enjoy Weinlesefest.

dialogues.speaker: Guy
dialogues.text: The happier everyone in town is, the more meaningless my day seems...

dialogues.speaker: Guy
dialogues.text: Weinlesefest. My father must be busy... What am I doing here? I might as well be at home helping.

dialogues.speaker: Athos
dialogues.text: Happy Weinlesefest! The Knights of Favonius are holding a charity sale at Cider Lake. All residents and visitors are welcome to participate!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hey, kiddo! Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: At the invitation of the Librarian, members of the Adventurers' Guild are expected to participate in Weinlesefest as well.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Enjoy the wine, enjoy the adventure and help all those in need! This is the spirit of our adventurers, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Susie
dialogues.text: Have you heard the wind of Windcoming Day?

dialogues.speaker: Susie
dialogues.text: It must be Lord Barbatos who has returned to the homeland with a breeze and has given his blessing to Monddstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Susie
dialogues.text: Lord Barbatos, please enjoy our wine and give your blessing to Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's Weinlesefest, but Diona is nowhere to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: After all, she is especially upset when it comes to times like this. In order to ensure that she's still with us, we decided to let her take a couple days off.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: So... would you like to buy me a special Weinlesefest drink?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Holidays when one can have a proper drink are such a rare occasion! Why don't we take a detour and buy some liquid refreshments... or maybe take a trip to Springvale?

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: I've never heard your voice before... Are you a traveler who came here to participate in Weinlesefest?

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Welcome. I hope you enjoy the festival as much as I do.

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Although I can't see to celebrate with everyone else, this festival brings me the best news of all: that all is well with the Knights of Favonius' expedition...

dialogues.speaker: Nelson
dialogues.text: Are you here for the limited-edition festival wine, too? Let's drink together. Come, come, have a seat!

dialogues.speaker: Nelson
dialogues.text: I wouldn't have expected less from the Dawn Winery's products. Every year, it arrives with the west wind and just gets more and more fragrant.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Hello friend. Have you heard of the ballad of the Windcoming Day?

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: The song of this festival is not only beautiful, but also seems to have a hidden deeper meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Sayid
dialogues.text: Like the secret to a good wine, it also contains the meaning of life... Mmm, that's good material.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Elzer...

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Ah, so you heard... Elzer is the executive chairman of the Mondstadt Wine Guild.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: This year, the Knights of Favonius, in collaboration with the Church of Favonius and the Adventurers' Guild, is hosting a Wine Market and are in need of a special budget.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: However, Elzer invited me to collaborate and he helped us solve a lot of our financial problems.

dialogues.speaker: Hertha
dialogues.text: Although he didn't say it explicitly... But my guess is that this grant came at the behest of a once senior Knight of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Elzer
dialogues.text: Oh? Distinguished guest, may I ask, are you here to discuss business?

dialogues.speaker: Elzer
dialogues.text: If it's for Weinlesefest, I've got Master's permission to do what I can to help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Master Kaeya?

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Looks like he's doing pretty well recently. Though he laughed all the way through dinner with Master Diluc, I could see that he was worried...

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: If you're asking about the title, that's all in the past...

dialogues.speaker: Adelinde
dialogues.text: Sorry, that was a slip of the tongue... Please forget I ever said that.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler. There's a big festival going on in Cider Lake, and there's been a lot more tourists in town lately.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: The festival is going well! My daughter is on a break, so I get to spend more time with her.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: I don't know if it's because his daughter is on break or what, but Draff has been extra jolly these days and is drinking even harder after work...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: It's a good thing that young one has been helping out lately, or I wouldn't be able to stand up if I had to hunt all by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Olaf
dialogues.text: Traveler! It's you! Welcome to Mondstadt's Weinlesefest.

dialogues.speaker: Olaf
dialogues.text: I really miss it... Although there seem to be few people brewing the "Thousand-Wind Wine" now, the return of the west wind is still so familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: There you are, dear Marvin.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Oh, Marla! I can't turn my back on you, not when you're inviting me to Weinlesefest!

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: No matter what your father thinks of us, my love... is like wine made from Mist Flowers...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla, no... Your love should not be a thing so cold...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: No. I mean that, my love will turn into burning liquor to warm you for a thousand — nay, for ten thousand years...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Oh, Marla, my love! Then my love for you is like the bitter north wind that follows the west wind...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Marvin, no... Your love should not be a thing so chilly...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: No. I mean that, I don't want you out of my sight, not even for a moment. I want to turn into a full season of Mondstadt's wind, always by your side...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Oh, Marvin!

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Oh, Marla!

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Master Goth pays me to protect his young esquire. His young esquire pays me to keep this a secret from his old man.

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: To get paid double, I just have to stay put and keep my mouth shut.

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Hmph, look at them. Being all lovey-dovey when I'm right here watching. Young people these days, no sense of shame...

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Wait a second... Are they getting a kick out of me watching them!?

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: ...Ugh, I cannot abide this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Scram!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you bored?

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Of course. After chasing the monsters away, I have absolutely nothing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Earlier, the young master asked me to help him pick some flowers, but he and that young lady started getting all lovey-dovey right away...

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: What need do they have for flowers? I reckon the young master's forgotten all about it already.

dialogues.speaker: Sharp
dialogues.text: Do you want them? Just take them if you do. They're no use to me, anyhow.
